title: Onramp pulse lane status notes — low-latency escalation and integration checks
content:
Weekly onramp pulse — 2029-04-09
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Leah, Ben, Ravi, Claire (customer success guest)
Meeting length: 40m
Purpose: quick sync on active integrations in the onramp lane; surface low-latency regressions, deployment handoffs, and immediate triage items for Dedicated/Private rollouts.

Agenda:
- Quick wins & greenlights (2 min)
- Customer-specific escalations (20 min)
- Platform/infra notes that impact onramp (8 min)
- Action items & owners (10 min)

Summary / quick bullets:
- Headline: p95 token latency for dedicated pool X increased ~18% since last Friday after the kernel update; investigating whether the new kernel schedule degrades short-sequence latency.
- Two customers (ValenceHealth, Meridian Bank) on private-beta are impacted for tail latency; both requested follow-up by EOD tomorrow.
- NovaRetail onboarding progressing; early traffic shows good throughput but intermittent 502s from the LB during heavy prefix-cache warmups.
- Rolling recommendation: pause kernel schedule change for non-critical fleets until we validate short-sequence perf on the canary host.

Customer updates (detailed)
1) ValenceHealth (Private VPC onramp) — contact: Claire / CS
   - Status: Blocker (tail latency)
   - Symptoms: Batch of low-QPS calls with short prompts (avg 32 tokens) returning p95 latency 480ms -> 560ms (was 470ms last week). Error rate nominal.
   - Recent change correlated: runtime kernel schedule bump (PR #4123) landed on the region pool used by Valence.
   - Investigation notes:
     - KV cache hit ratio for Valence is >92% (their prompts are highly templated) — caching seems OK.
     - Profiling shows higher scheduler wake cost on short sequences with the new kernel path (scheduling overhead added ~40–60us per token).
     - Hypothesis: new micro-batching thresholds push short requests into a slightly different codepath that adds latency.
   - Next steps: revert kernel schedule on their Dedicated pool for 24h and run A/B with canary. Miguel to coordinate with infra.
   - Owner: Miguel Santos, ETA: 2029-04-10 EOD

2) Meridian Bank (Dedicated w/ Reserved capacity) — contact: Priya (Acct)
   - Status: Elevated (customer worried about p95 SLOs)
   - Symptoms: periodic spikes in p95 during hourly batch job that floods the pool (internal ingestion). Observed queuing >120ms for bursts.
   - Mitigations tried: burst autoscale allowed but warmup latency still visible. We suspect autoscale policy needs pre-warming for scheduled ingestion windows.
   - Short-term ask: create scheduled warmup policy (pre-launch warmup 5 minutes before ingestion) and increase burst headroom by 10%.
   - Owner: Leah Cho + Product (dedicated autoscale config), ETA: 2029-04-11 morning

3) NovaRetail (Hosted -> Dedicated pilot) — contact: Daniel (SE/Customer)
   - Status: Progressing, intermittent 502s from LB during first-hour traffic ramp.
   - Symptoms: 502s coincide with heavy prefix cache population and sudden spike in ephemeral worker spin-ups. Error is at loadbalancer layer, not model.
   - Short-term workaround: stagger client ramp by 10s backoff and add a short retry wrapper in their SDK. Ben to draft recommended SDK snippet.
   - Long-term: increase backend connection pool and tune LB health probe thresholds for warmup windows.
   - Owner: Ben Hart, ETA: SDK snippet by 2029-04-10; infra ticket for LB tuning created (JIRA-SE-2214).

Platform / infra notes affecting onramp
- Kernel PR #4123: landed Tuesday night. Canary hosts showed inconclusive gains for long sequences but small regressions for short sequences. Recommendation from runtime team: freeze rollout for non-critical pools.
- KV cache prefill improvements: new prefill heuristics will be toggled in opt-in mode for one customer next week (NovaRetail) — expect fewer warmup 502s once in place.
- Routing & fallbacks: found one account (internal test account) with misconfigured fallback policy that caused calls to route to an incompatible quantized variant — fixed live. Audit script to run nightly for the next week.
- Observability: Console traces show increased tail on the scheduling stage; tracing link posted to the GitHub PR for deeper profiling.

Open action items (short list)
- Miguel: Coordinate rollback of kernel schedule for ValenceHealth dedicated pool; confirm after A/B test and report findings. (Due 2029-04-10 EOD)
- Leah: Implement scheduled warmup policy template and push a one-click config to the console for Dedicated customers with scheduled ingestion. (Due 2029-04-11)
- Ben: Publish SDK retry backoff snippet and include guidance for ramping traffic; add example in the NovaRetail onboarding doc. (Due 2029-04-10)
- Ravi: Add nightly audit job to validate fallback routing policies and produce a weekly report. (Due 2029-04-12)
- Aisha: Draft customer-facing note for Valence & Meridian summarizing investigation and mitigation steps; share with CS for approval. (Due 2029-04-10 morning)

Risks & asks
- Ask to Product (Leah / Priya): consider temporary SLA credit for Meridian if p95 SLOs breach next window while we roll out pre-warming.
- Risk: If kernel schedule rollback is refused by runtime team, we will need a targeted micro-patch to re-align short-sequence path — estimated dev effort 3 days.

Notes / miscellaneous
- Quick win: small prompt engineering tweak suggested to Valence (reduce needless system tokens) cut their median token count by ~6 tokens in test, shaving ~12ms median latency.
- FYI: Claire (CS) wants a one-pager for execs summarizing status across the three customers by Monday. Aisha to draft.

Next meeting: 2029-04-16, same time, if any critical items arise we'll schedule an ad-hoc warroom.

Appendix: quick references
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
- Infra ticket for LB tuning: JIRA-SE-2214
- Canary tracing snapshot: confluence:Onramp-Network-Checklist

——
Notes capture style: working doc — rough action list, experimental hypotheses, and short-form notes intended to be iterated in next sync.
